result_text:
`analyzeLandscape` is now a second name for `updateLandscape`, and the CLI module compiles offline. I could not run the built command to check the output, because executing the compiled class needed approval I couldn't get here. The `-help` and dispatch behaviour below is verified by reading the code only.

Changes:

- **`cli/.../Commands.java`**: added `ANALYZE_LANDSCAPE` and its description, which calls it the landscape counterpart of the analysis commands and the same as `updateLandscape`. It is listed in the no-argument overview right after `updateLandscape`, using the same landscape options.
- **`cli/.../CommandLineInterface.java`**:
  - Both names dispatch to the same `updateLandscape(args)` method, so options and behaviour are identical.
  - `-help` now prints usage under the name the user typed (`args[0]`), with the matching description. `updateLandscape -help` still prints its own usage.
- **`README.md`**: the README had no command descriptions, so I added a short "Landscape report" section covering `analyzeLandscape`, `updateLandscape` as the kept alias, the output paths, and `-help`.

I did not touch `CLAUDE.md`, which still lists only `updateLandscape` among the main commands. The cli module has no tests, so none were run. Nothing is committed.
